posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
I've got a subject that I want to make a hologram of. Trouble is, it's chrome globe with the continents painted in.

I've tried putting it into an environment where the chrome works naturally but I can't get the right lighting combination that will make this work.

Does anyone have a recommendation for a removable (in water preferably) coating that will diffuse the illumation light so that the globe is less of a mirror?

posts.author: Kaveh
posts.content_md: Don't know how to do that, but have you thought of using a very diffuse illumination beam? That would reduce the specular reflections from the globe.

posts.author: Guest
posts.content_md: Colin had previously posted about a "flatting" spary or something like that which is used in theatrics...

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
You mean this post...

[http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewt ... 2532#12532](http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?p=12532#12532)

I can't use that spray since I'd end up cleaning the original paint off but hairspray might work.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Flatting spray is simply clear laquer with a flatting agent. You can make your own if you have a air brush. It does not wash off. Hairspray is very similiar. Test your brand as it can be hard to wash off.

posts.author: BobH
posts.content_md: There is certainly water soluable dulling spray. Try art stores. After dulling, I'd use big diffused light as suggested by Keveh and cut the specular reflection down with polarization manipulation.

posts.author: Gary Deal
posts.content_md: Years ago I saw a tip for dulling silverware in product photography without making them look too dull. Spray anti-perspirant. (Does that even exist anymore?) The stuff would go on and create a more diffuse surface, and easily wash/wipe off.

posts.author: MarkCavin
posts.content_md: How about some of that chalk dust athletes grind in their hands? Or grind up the color(s) of your choice from your kids chalk sticks. Then dust your object.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
dust would just slide off the chrome.

I'll definitely try some of the other suggestions and let the group know what worked and didn't.

posts.author: MarkCavin
posts.content_md: Shine the raw object beam onto a aspirin tablet and let it diffuse the light?

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
That works as a reflector but not for my setup which needs a transmissive diffusor.

Fortunately I've got a good selection of objects that work well. Milk jug bits, broken bulbs, etc.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: How about using a water based, washable paint to paint the reflective spots. I am assuming the continents are not reflective. This would take time but the object can be soaked and cleaned easily. If they contents are also reflective you could paint them also. I did a similar hologram years ago and want to recreate it in DCG. What I did and it worked pretty good, was to get a light fixture globe, which was glass and paint the continents on it. Then I could made letters out of balsa wood which I placed inside that read, "Save the Earth". Anywhere there was not a continent you could read the lettering inside. Good luck.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> How about using a water based, washable paint to paint the reflective spots.

I tried something like that last night. The chrome's too smooth and the liquid just beads up.

I've had a chance to experiment and it looks like the winner will be a combination of hirspray and talcum powder.

I did cycles of spraying on hairspray and blowing powder onto the wet spray. Looks pretty good under laser light so far. I'll let everyone know how it turns out.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
Well, the hologram itself has an odd dark band across the middle, as though the plate moved during exposure but the left edge is nice and bright and clear.

Where the globe shows, it is clearly visible. The hairspray and talc combination is a roaring success. Thanks everyone for the tips. I'll post pictures as soon as I figure out where that dark band is coming from.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md: For future reference, I was just going through my paint collection and found a can of Krylon 41310 "Removable Dulling Spray (semi-drying)". It seems to contains petroleum distillates and is not compatible wth all materials, but is claimed removable - instructions state "rub gently under running water or sponge with a wet cloth". Have not tried removing yet. Got it at an art supply store.
